title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Which Charges a Settlement Takes In
content:
**Judgement 1.** Where charges stand on the program that have not fallen due within the ledger window of
24 months and charges also stand that have fallen due within it, every charge invoiced on the program is
taken in, fallen due or not.

**Judgement 2.** Where no charge on the program has fallen due within that ledger window but charges
stand that have not, only the charges that have not fallen due within it are taken in.

**Judgement 3.** In any other case neither judgement above widens or narrows the charges taken in.

| Charges that have fallen due within the 24-month ledger window | Charges that have not fallen due within it | What is taken in |
|---|---|---|
| some stand | some stand | every charge invoiced on the program, fallen due or not |
| none stands | some stand | only the charges that have not fallen due within it |
| some stand | none stands | neither judgement above widens or narrows what is taken in |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** A rate program under the Demand Service Rate Programs carries 7000 US
dollars of charges that fell due inside the 24 months and 900 US dollars raised in the billing month
that have not fallen due. Every charge is taken in, so 7900 US dollars stands. Where the same program
carried only the 900 US dollars that have not fallen due and nothing that fell due inside the window,
900 US dollars would be taken in.
